sources.note: Parts 1 and 2 use everyday contexts. Part 3 uses an educational or training discussion between two main speakers, sometimes guided by a tutor. Part 4 is an academic monologue. Original scripts currently require supervised live delivery.

sources.subject: Listening
sources.note: The 2026 blueprint identifies Listen and Choose a Response, Listen to a Conversation, Listen to an Announcement and Listen to an Academic Talk. The Listening webpage lists all four despite its introductory phrase saying two task types. This batch uses original single-exchange response practice with four written response choices, as illustrated in the official Updated Test Overview p. 9. Adaptive assembly, recorded delivery and scaled scores remain outside the draft batch. The official Updated Test Overview p. 9 specifies a short two-speaker conversation with two questions, including inference, intent and likely next actions. The regional mirror was used after the German mirror exceeded the retrieval size limit. Updated Test Overview p. 11 describes announcements of about 40–85 words and shows four answer choices. It does not specify a fixed question count per announcement in the retrieved passage. Two practice questions per original announcement are an author choice. Updated Test Overview p. 12 specifies academic talks of about 100–250 words with four questions and no required background knowledge.

sources.note: Correct the historical curriculum spelling Lord Laggard to Frederick Lugard. The distinction is recorded, not silently substituted.
